Safety filters automatically redact sensitive data before it reaches the model, so they duplicate Model Armor

stem: A research lab can train a model either on its own Compute Engine GPU VMs or with managed custom training on Agent Platform. Compared with the managed option, which security responsibility does the self-managed Compute Engine option add for the lab?

choices.text: Hardening and patching the guest OS image, limiting the VM's network exposure and choosing the identity it uses
Encrypting data at rest, which Compute Engine leaves unencrypted unless the lab enables a key
Defining IAM roles for the training service, which exist only when the lab runs its own Compute Engine instances
Securing the physical GPU hosts and the hypervisor underneath the VMs

stem: After a perimeter and restricted VIP were enabled, a team's Agent Platform Pipelines component fails: it installs Python packages from the internet at run time. The pipeline runs in a Google-managed producer network that the perimeter now locks down. What is the recommended fix?

choices.text: Add a default route back to the internet gateway in the producer network so that package downloads work again
Grant the pipeline's service account the owner role so that installations can bypass the perimeter
Bake the dependencies into a container image for the component so nothing is installed at run time
Remove the Agent Platform API from the perimeter permanently, then run pipelines unprotected

stem: A hospital's data scientists use Agent Platform Workbench instances on PHI. The security engineer wants memory encryption for notebook processing, notebook traffic inside the organization's service perimeter, and keys the hospital controls. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: Keep the default Google-managed network, enable only CMEK, and rely on IAM for every other requirement
Enable Confidential Computing after creation by editing the running instance, and leave the network default
Use Shielded VM, which gives memory encryption, and remove the instances from the VPC to avoid exposure
Create instances with Confidential Computing enabled, on a specified VPC within the service perimeter, and use CMEK

stem: A team deploys an agent on Agent Platform Runtime that can call tools reading customer records. A red team shows that a poisoned web page can steer the agent into calling tools it should not. Which combination limits impact best?

choices.text: Share one broad service account among all agents to simplify audits, with network firewall rules as the control
Give the agent its own least-privilege identity for its tools and data, and screen traffic with Model Armor
Run the agent as a project owner so that tool calls never fail, and add more logging of its outputs
Rely on the model's system instructions to forbid misuse, since the model follows instructions reliably

stem: A platform team wants a Cloud Build pipeline to stop an image from reaching Artifact Registry if it contains HIGH or CRITICAL vulnerabilities. The image should be scanned before it is pushed. Which design fits?

choices.text: Run a weekly Security Command Center report and have engineers manually delete vulnerable images
Rely on automatic scanning in Artifact Registry, which scans the image after the push and can reject it during the upload
Add a Binary Authorization attestor that scans the source code repository and signs each commit
Add a build step that runs On-Demand Scanning on the built image, checks the severities, and fails the build before the push step

stem: A base image was pushed to Artifact Registry eight months ago and has since been used only by a long-running service that is never restarted. A new critical CVE affecting a package in the image is announced, yet the image shows no new finding. What explains this?

choices.text: Continuous analysis keeps updating only images pulled in the last 30 days; after that their metadata goes stale
Automatic scanning scans an image only once per tag, so renaming the tag would never produce a new result
New CVEs are only applied to images that were scanned on demand, so the registry copy needs a manual scan
Artifact Analysis cannot detect vulnerabilities in operating system packages, only those in application libraries

stem: A security director with 300 projects wants one place to see which container images with known vulnerabilities exist across the organization, ranked with other risks, and to keep the data for analysis. What should the engineer set up?

choices.text: Ask each project owner to email a weekly spreadsheet of scan results to a central mailbox
Create one Cloud Build trigger per project that prints findings to the build logs for later review
Enable Artifact Registry scanning and use Security Command Center, which aggregates findings and exports them to BigQuery
Run On-Demand Scanning from one project against images in every other project, as results stay stored centrally for a year

stem: After a company enables SAML single sign-on between Cloud Identity and its corporate IdP, a newly hired engineer authenticates successfully at the IdP but Google sign-in rejects the assertion. The IdP sends the engineer's employee number as the NameID, and a Cloud Identity user with the engineer's email address exists. What is the most likely cause and fix?

choices.text: The IdP signing certificate has to be uploaded to the engineer's user profile instead of to the single sign-on profile
The engineer must be added to a super admin group, because only super admins can be matched to assertions from an IdP
The engineer's Cloud Identity user must first be given a password, which Google compares with the one entered at the IdP
The NameID must match the user's primary email address in Cloud Identity, so the IdP must be configured to send that value

stem: A web application lets employees sign in with their Google identity. Its backend must learn which user is interacting with it, and it never calls a Google API on the user's behalf. Which token should the backend verify, and why?

choices.text: The user ID token, a signed JWT issued to that client, which identifies the user but cannot call Google APIs
A service account ID token, because identity tokens are always issued for workloads and never for human users
The user access token, because each access token carries a readable copy of the signed-in user's full profile
The refresh token, because it is the only token type that is tied to the identity of the user who authorized the client

stem: A security team reviews what a stolen laptop exposes in an internal tool that uses OAuth. Employees who sign in as Cloud Identity users hold refresh tokens, and contractors who come through a workforce identity pool hold federated refresh tokens. Which statement about cutting off these tokens is accurate?

choices.text: Both kinds are revoked in the same way, so one offboarding procedure for tokens covers employees and contractors
A refresh token can be revoked, but a federated refresh token cannot and stays valid until its workforce identity session expires
A refresh token expires within an hour, like an ID token, so a stolen laptop exposes the employee only briefly
A federated refresh token can be used once, like an authorization code, so a stolen copy is worthless after one exchange

stem: An enterprise syncs users from Active Directory into Cloud Identity and enables SAML SSO with AD FS. The security architect must decide where password complexity rules and MFA are managed for employees signing in to the Google Cloud console. Where does that responsibility sit?

choices.text: With IAM, because allow policies define password length and MFA requirements per principal
With the Google Cloud console, because it applies its own MFA prompt to every federated sign-in regardless of the IdP
With the on-premises identity system, because passwords are not synchronized and sign-in is delegated to it through SAML
With Cloud Identity, because synchronization copies password hashes to Google so that Google can validate them

stem: A holding company has two subsidiaries. The first needs mandatory SAML SSO through its own IdP; the second has no IdP and wants Google-managed passwords with 2-Step Verification. The architect prefers a single Cloud Identity account. What constraint must be weighed?

choices.text: SSO is an account-wide setting for all users except super admins, so mixed models need scoping or separate accounts
SSO applies only to users holding an organization-level IAM role, so the second subsidiary is automatically excluded
SSO is applied per project, so each subsidiary can set its own policy simply by having its own project
SSO applies to Google Cloud console sign-in but not to the Admin console, so both subsidiaries can share one authentication model

stem: Which TWO statements about a SAML-federated Cloud Identity deployment are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Google stores a hash of each employee's IdP password to validate sign-ins during an IdP outage
Directory synchronization from Active Directory to Cloud Identity is bidirectional
The IdP authenticates the user and applies its MFA policy before Google trusts the sign-in
A user without a counterpart in the IdP can still sign in by using a password stored in Google
Users are redirected to the IdP after entering their primary email address in the Google sign-in prompt

stem: A developer runs a script with a user access token. A colleague argues that because the user holds the Storage Admin role on a project, the token will always be able to list every bucket in it. A security engineer explains that this need not be true. Why?

choices.text: OAuth scopes replace IAM roles, so a token without the storage scope removes the role from the user's allow policy
A user access token is restricted to the OAuth scopes it was issued with, and IAM still decides which permissions apply
User access tokens never expire, so the role used at issue time is checked once and then cached indefinitely
Access tokens are issued to the project rather than to a client, so they carry whichever role the project default has

stem: A security team wants to reduce the damage from a leaked access token that was captured from a developer laptop. Which property of Google Cloud tokens most directly limits the damage window?

choices.text: Access tokens are signed with the developer's SSH key, so they cannot be replayed elsewhere
Access tokens are single-use and are rejected by the second API call that presents them
Access tokens are stored in Cloud KMS and are automatically destroyed 90 days after issue
Access tokens are short-lived and expire within hours, so a stolen one soon stops working

stem: A nightly job must read Google Workspace data that IAM roles on Google Cloud cannot grant, and an engineer proposes a service account with domain-wide delegation. Which TWO statements follow Google's guidance? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Delegate to a super admin user so that the job keeps working whichever Workspace API it needs later
Prefer domain-wide delegation for web applications that act for users, because it avoids asking those users for consent
Keep one shared service user in Cloud Identity for all applications, and leave it out of the IdP so that IdP changes cannot affect it
Use domain-wide delegation only when end-user consent through OAuth 2.0 is not practical, because delegation is a powerful privilege
Delegate to a dedicated Cloud Identity user that is created in the IdP and provisioned, so Cloud Identity stays a subset of the IdP

stem: Only 150 of 6,000 employees will ever use Google Cloud or other Google services, and the company federates Cloud Identity with its IdP. The architect wants an extra layer of defense in case an access rule is accidentally too lax. What should be done?

choices.text: Create Cloud Identity users only for those 150 employees, and allow only them to sign in to Google through SSO at the IdP
Create Cloud Identity users for all 6,000 employees and rely on IAM roles to withhold access from everyone who does not need it
Create no Cloud Identity users and let the first SSO sign-in of any IdP user create a matching Google account
Create Cloud Identity users for all 6,000 employees and keep the other 5,850 only in a suspended group at the IdP

stem: A platform team grants broad roles to developers but must stop anyone, other than members of a project-admins group, from deleting projects tagged env=prod, without editing every role grant. Which control fits best?

choices.text: A custom role for developers that omits the project-delete permission, swapped into every existing role binding in every project
An organization policy constraint that lists the group as the only principal able to delete projects
A deny policy on the project-delete permission with a tag-based denial condition and the group as exception principal
An allow policy condition on each developer's role binding that checks the project tag

stem: To limit damage from phished credentials and data exfiltration, a company wants its employees and service accounts to be unable to use their roles on resources that belong to other organizations, even where those organizations' allow policies grant them access. Which control fits?

choices.text: A deny policy on the company's organization that names every external organization's projects as denied resources
A Principal Access Boundary policy listing the company's organization as eligible resources, bound to its principals
An allow policy condition on every role binding that checks the parent organization of the requested resource
An organization policy constraint that lists the external organizations whose resources company users may not call

stem: Contractors hold Compute Instance Admin on a project, and the company wants to block those same permissions outside business hours and on weekends. A colleague proposes a deny policy with a denial condition that tests the request time. Why does this fail, and what is the right way?

choices.text: Denial conditions accept every attribute allowed in allow policies, so the proposal works if the expression is on the permission name
Deny rules cannot target contractor groups, so convert the contractors to service accounts and deny those
Denial conditions recognize only resource tag functions, so use conditional role bindings on request.time for the contractors' allow grants
Request time can be tested only in organization policies, so create a constraint that covers working hours

stem: Which TWO statements about IAM deny rules are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A wildcard permission group denies current and future permissions that match the pattern for that resource type
A principal can lift a deny by holding the Owner role on the project where the deny applies
A denial condition that cannot be evaluated is treated as false, so the rule does not apply
Deny policies can be attached to a single Cloud Storage object, giving per-object guardrails
Exception principals are exempt even if they belong to a group that is named as a denied principal

stem: A support group needs to restart only Compute Engine instances whose names begin with "stg-" in a shared project, and nothing else. Granting a role on each instance is rejected because many instances are created dynamically. How can least privilege still be achieved?

choices.text: Grant a custom role with every Compute permission and place the group in a stricter folder
Grant the role at the project with an IAM condition on the resource name prefix and resource type
Grant the role on the organization so that the condition is inherited by every project
Grant the Editor basic role to the group and rely on audit logs to detect misuse

stem: A company hosts an internal admin app behind Identity-Aware Proxy. Access to it should be given only to the admin group and only when requests come from managed corporate devices. Which IAM approach expresses this?

choices.text: Use an organization policy constraint that restricts the app to a list of approved laptop device identifiers
Add a deny policy that blocks the group from the app unless the request time is within office hours
Grant the group the Compute Viewer role at the project and rely on the VM firewall to check the device
Bind the IAP web app user role to the group with a condition that requires an Access Context Manager access level

stem: A security engineer says: "Access Context Manager does not itself block any request." Which description of the service is accurate?

choices.text: It enforces access levels on every API call and writes each denial to Cloud Audit Logs
It stores IAM allow policies for the organization and evaluates them on each request
It is a firewall service that filters packets between VPC networks
It defines access levels and service perimeters; VPC Service Controls and others enforce them

stem: An SRE team must be able to fix production incidents at 3 a.m. without waiting for a manager, but the company wants every use of elevated access justified and auditable, and no standing admin rights. Which Privileged Access Manager design fits?

choices.text: A deny policy that blocks the SRE group's permissions until a ticket number is attached to the support case
An entitlement that requires two levels of approval from directors who work only in business hours
An entitlement for the SRE group with the role, a required justification, a short maximum duration and no approval
A permanent role binding for the SRE group with a condition that expires after one year

stem: A regulator requires that no single administrator can both request and approve high-risk production changes, and that approval chains be automated where a change ticket exists. Which Privileged Access Manager capability supports this?

choices.text: Multi-level, multi-party approvals, with service accounts as approvers that validate tickets
Grant retention that keeps denied requests in Cloud Audit Logs forever
A custom role without approve permissions attached to the requester group
A grant scheduled seven days ahead that approves itself as soon as the request is created by the engineer

stem: A team tries to turn its standing project Owner role into a temporary Privileged Access Manager entitlement, but the Owner role cannot be selected. What is the correct solution?

choices.text: Create the entitlement at the Cloud Storage bucket level, where Owner is accepted
Choose a predefined or custom role, since the legacy basic roles are not supported by entitlements
Attach the entitlement to a service account, as only service accounts may receive basic roles
Wait 30 days for the entitlement to mature, after which every role is supported

stem: Privileged Access Manager grants on a project behave erratically: some elevated access never appears and some persists after expiry. An administrator discovers that automation re-applies the project's allow policy from source control every hour. What is the explanation?

choices.text: PAM adds and removes time-conditioned bindings in the allow policy, and outside edits break this
PAM grants are applied through organization policies, which source control overrides
PAM stores grants in a separate permission store that is bypassed by allow policy writes
PAM grants are cached on the requester's laptop until the next sign-in, so expiry depends on it

stem: A team currently gives on-call engineers a role binding with an IAM condition that expires at the end of each quarter. The security lead wants approvals, justifications and a record of who used which access. Why is Privileged Access Manager a better fit than conditional bindings alone?

choices.text: It makes the grants permanent so that engineers no longer have to renew them each quarter
It adds justification, optional approval and audit logging; a conditional binding only expires
It replaces IAM Conditions, which can no longer be used for time-based expiry
It grants the role to every principal in the organization so requesters need no individual lookup

stem: IAM recommender suggests removing a data-reader role from a team on a bucket. The bucket also has object ACLs that give the same team access, and the owner worries that applying the suggestion might break access or leave it hidden. What should the security engineer conclude?

choices.text: Applying the recommendation also deletes the object ACLs, which prevents any residual access
ACL grants are merged into IAM policies automatically, so the suggestion already counts every ACL entry
Recommendations never apply to Cloud Storage, so the suggestion can be ignored
Recommendations consider only IAM, not ACLs, so ACL grants need a manual review

stem: A Principal Access Boundary policy makes the company's service accounts eligible to access only the company's own organization. A red-team test shows that a service account still performs one particular action on a resource in another organization, although most cross-organization actions are now blocked. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: Principal Access Boundary policies are advisory only: they write violations to audit logs and never block a request
The role binding that grants the access is evaluated first and overrides the boundary for roles granted directly
The policy's enforcement version cannot block the permission behind that action, so the policy has no effect on it
Principal Access Boundary policies apply only to human users, so a service account is never subject to them

stem: Developers should hold a deployment role only on resources tagged env=dev, across 60 projects under one folder. When a project owner changes a resource's tag, developer access must follow automatically, without anyone editing an IAM policy. Which design fits?

choices.text: Grant the role to the developers group on the folder, with a condition that tests the resource's env tag for the value dev
Grant the role to the developers group on each project, with a condition on a resource name prefix that marks the dev resources
Grant the role to each developer on every dev resource individually, and rerun a script whenever any tag changes
Grant the role to the developers group on the folder, and add a deny policy that lists the project IDs of the 60 projects

stem: Which TWO statements describe how an organization should use Policy Simulator before tightening access? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Use the simulator instead of audit logs to detect past unauthorized access
Simulate a change and treat the result as covering allow, deny and Principal Access Boundary policies at once
Simulate a proposed deny policy to see which principals would lose access before attaching it
Use the simulator to enforce the change at the same time
Simulate replacing a broad role with a narrower one to check whether the principal's actual access would change

stem: Which TWO statements about IAM Conditions are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A condition needs both a title and a description, and a binding with a missing description is rejected
Condition expressions accept the full Common Expression Language specification, so any CEL function can be used
Conditions can be used only in allow policy role bindings and are not available in deny rules or Principal Access Boundary bindings
To match resource names, write a startsWith() or endsWith() test, because wildcard characters such as * are not supported
Only some resource types accept conditions in their own role bindings, so access to the others is made conditional by granting at the project or organization

stem: A project IAM review finds individual users bound directly to roles in dozens of projects, and several teams hold Owner on their projects. The organization wants maintainable least privilege that supports both separation of duties and easy offboarding. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Grant Owner to one group at the organization root so every project inherits one policy
Bind narrow predefined roles to groups at small scope, and use Project IAM Admin instead of Owner
Keep user-level bindings on every project but export the allow policies weekly to review them
Replace all roles with one custom role holding each permission any team uses

stem: A security team enforced the organization policy constraint that denies external IPv4 addresses on VM instances across the production folder. A later scan shows that a few VMs in dual-stack subnets are still reachable from the internet through external IPv6 addresses. What explains this, and what closes the gap?

choices.text: The constraint takes effect only for VMs created after enforcement, so recreate the VMs and the external IPv6 addresses will be removed automatically
The constraint is overridden by default for any VM that has a service account attached, so remove the service accounts from the affected VMs
The constraint covers IPv6 only when the subnet is in custom mode, so convert every dual-stack subnet in the folder to custom mode and re-apply it
The constraint governs only IPv4 external addresses, so keep private workloads on subnets with internal IPv6 access and deny ingress with firewall rules

stem: A bank's proxy team must let developers download packages from www.example.com/documentation but block www.example.com/uploads, for HTTPS traffic leaving private VMs through Secure Web Proxy. All VMs are managed by the bank. Which configuration meets the requirement?

choices.text: Enable TLS inspection with a CA Service CA pool, install the root certificate on the managed VMs, and write path-based URL rules
Switch the proxy to next hop mode, because that mode decrypts HTTPS traffic natively so that full URLs become visible to rules
Add a hostname-only rule for www.example.com and rely on the HTTPS server name to separate the documentation path from the uploads path
Add a gateway security rule that matches the destination IP address of www.example.com, allowing one path and blocking the other path

stem: After a bank enabled Secure Web Proxy TLS inspection for all outbound HTTPS from managed VMs, operating system and browser updates fail with certificate errors, while ordinary websites work. The applications are known to accept only specific public CA chains. What is the best fix?

choices.text: Install the proxy's private root CA on the update servers operated by the vendors, so that they trust the certificates the proxy issues
Turn off TLS inspection for the whole policy until the vendors of the update clients start accepting the proxy's private CA certificates
Add the update hostnames to the session matcher as exclusions so those connections bypass decryption, and keep inspection for everything else
Move the VMs to a subnet that sends traffic to Cloud NAT directly, which restores update access but still lets the proxy log the sessions

stem: A network security engineer reviews the properties of Secure Web Proxy before approving it for a Shared VPC environment. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Source-based rules can match only IP addresses, so identity-based rules require a separate identity-aware proxy product
A proxy instance can be deployed only in the host project, not in a service project
TLS inspection works without any client configuration, even from unmanaged devices that lack the private root CA
Secure Web Proxy supports HTTP/3 and IPv6 traffic, so QUIC-based applications pass through the proxy unchanged
Outbound traffic is denied by default until a gateway security rule explicitly allows it

stem: A company enabled DNSSEC on the Cloud DNS public zone for example.org and the console shows it as on. A security scan using a validating resolver still reports that the domain has no chain of trust. The registrar is a small reseller. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: No DS record was published at the registrar for the parent zone, so resolvers cannot link the signed zone to the registry
Cloud DNS signs only records of type A, so the NS and MX records in the zone are unsigned and break validation for the whole zone
The zone keys must be rotated manually before validating resolvers accept them, and no rotation has been performed yet
DNSSEC works only for private zones, so enabling it on a public managed zone has no effect on public resolvers

stem: A security team wants every VM in a VPC network to receive a sinkhole address for any lookup of *.malware-campaign.test, while one required subdomain, updates.malware-campaign.test, must still resolve normally through the existing private zone. How should the team implement this with Cloud DNS?

choices.text: Create a DNS routing policy on the wildcard record set with weighted round robin so that most answers resolve to the sinkhole address
Apply an inbound server policy on the network so that the sinkhole answers are served to every VM that uses the metadata server
Attach a response policy to the network with a wildcard rule returning the sinkhole address and a passthru rule for the one subdomain
Create a DNSSEC-signed public zone for the domain that contains the sinkhole records, so validating resolvers return those records

stem: A security operations team suspects that a compromised GKE workload uses DNS lookups of random-looking names to exfiltrate data, and queries are resolved by the VPC network's resolver. The team wants a record of every query the VPC resolves, kept in the project that owns the network. What should be configured?

choices.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs on the subnets, because flow logs contain the names that VMs and containers queried
Enable Packet Mirroring on the GKE nodes and store the mirrored traffic in a bucket, because Cloud DNS offers no logging
Create a log sink for Cloud Audit Logs Data Access in the project, because DNS queries are administrative API calls
Enable query logging in a Cloud DNS policy applied to the VPC network and analyze the records in Cloud Logging

stem: A platform team sets the Restrict Resource Service Usage constraint on the sandbox folder with a denylist containing compute.googleapis.com, meaning to stop VM creation. Teams then report that GKE cluster operations in the folder also fail, and the team wants to understand and roll out changes safely. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The constraint blocks runtime access for services such as IAM, Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring as well, because it covers every API
Applying the constraint with tags for conditional enforcement allows a staged rollout to selected projects before it is applied folder-wide
A policy can combine a denylist and an allowlist at the same level, so exceptions are written as allowed values within the denied list
Restricted services remain visible in the console, and only API calls to them fail
Services with a direct dependency on a restricted service are restricted as well, so Google Kubernetes Engine fails when Compute Engine is denied

stem: A mobile team embeds an API key for the Places API in a published Android app. A security review notes the key could be extracted and abused to run other APIs and consume quota. Which TWO controls limit what a stolen key can do? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Apply an organization policy to the project that disables the Places API for all keys, then test usage
Add an API restriction so the key can call only the Places API in the project
Keep the key but store it in Secret Manager, which prevents the app from sending it to Google APIs in a request
Replace the key with an IAM role on the app's users, because API keys are checked by IAM and need no restriction
Add an application restriction to the Android package name and signing certificate fingerprint

stem: A company has an enforced VPC Service Controls perimeter around its analytics projects. The security team wants to add the Cloud KMS API as a restricted service and also loosen an access level that admits the corporate IP range. They want to see the effect on production traffic first, with no risk of new denials. Which approach is correct?

choices.text: Edit the enforced configuration directly, because access level changes take effect only after a one-hour review period that works as a built-in test
Edit the access level in place and use the dry run perimeter configuration to test it, because access levels have a dry run mode of their own
Edit the dry run configuration, create a new access level reflecting the loosening and apply it to the dry run spec, then review dry run audit log entries
Clone the whole organization into a test organization and replay the production traffic there, because dry run cannot cover service changes

stem: A research partner's service account, which lives in the partner's own organization, must read one BigQuery dataset in a project protected by an enforced perimeter, running its query jobs in that same project, and nothing else. The partner's callers come from changing cloud IP addresses. What is the most precise configuration?

choices.text: An ingress rule naming that service account, with BigQuery read methods and only the project that holds the dataset as its target
An access level for the partner's IP ranges attached to the perimeter, because IP-based admission is the finest control available
A perimeter bridge between the perimeters of the two organizations, because bridges are the supported way to share across organizations
A second perimeter for the partner containing the project, so both organizations share one security boundary and one policy

stem: An analyst in a project outside an enforced perimeter runs a BigQuery query job in that outside project against a dataset in a project inside the perimeter. An ingress rule for the analyst was added, yet the query is still denied. Which TWO changes are needed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add the analyst's project as a service project of the perimeter project through a Shared VPC attachment
Replace the ingress rule with an access level on the analyst's device, because ingress rules cannot match user identities
Grant the analyst the BigQuery Admin role in the perimeter project, because IAM roles are evaluated before the perimeter
Add an egress rule that allows the BigQuery job project outside the perimeter to be used with the dataset inside it
Keep the ingress rule that lets the analyst's identity call BigQuery in the perimeter project

stem: A perimeter protects the service projects of a Shared VPC deployment. After enforcement, VMs in some service projects lose access to the Cloud Storage API, and requests show up as violations. The host project that owns the Shared VPC network sits outside every perimeter. What should the security engineer do?

choices.text: Create egress rules from the perimeter to the host project, since the host project is a Google-managed service project
Remove the service projects from the perimeter and protect them only with firewall rules on the host project's network
Add each service project to its own perimeter, and connect the perimeters with bridges so that each pair can communicate
Add the host project to the same perimeter as the service projects, so that the network and its workloads share one boundary

stem: A developer's VM in project dev-sandbox, which is outside any perimeter, cannot read a bucket in the perimeter-protected project prod-data. The audit log entry shows the violation reason NETWORK_NOT_IN_SAME_SERVICE_PERIMETER with a private caller IP address and a caller network. Developers must still be able to do this for a defined set of service accounts. What is the best resolution?

choices.text: Move the VM's project into the perimeter without any other review, since that removes the violation at once for every identity
Create an ingress rule whose source is the project that owns the caller network, restricted to the approved service accounts and storage methods
Add an access level with the VM's private IP range to the perimeter, because the access level then identifies the caller
Disable restricted services for Cloud Storage in the perimeter, so that the bucket can be read from any network

stem: Workloads in a perimeter-protected VPC network should be able to call only Cloud Storage and BigQuery APIs. Every other Google API, including Pub/Sub, should be refused from inside the network even though they could be used elsewhere in the organization. Which perimeter feature provides this?

choices.text: VPC accessible services configured with an allowlist of the Cloud Storage and BigQuery services
A perimeter bridge to a project that contains only Cloud Storage and BigQuery resources
A DNS response policy that returns no answer for the Pub/Sub API name but allows storage.googleapis.com
An access level that admits only requests whose caller IP range is part of the VPC network's subnets

stem: A company with one organization-level access policy has business units that each want to define and test their own perimeters for projects under their folder. The central security team does not want to hand out administration of the organization-wide policy. What should the security engineer use?

choices.text: Perimeter bridges managed by the business units, so each unit controls the traffic between its projects
One perimeter per business unit in the organization-level policy, with the unit's admins granted the organization role
A scoped access policy for each business unit's folder, with the administration role granted on that policy
A second organization-level access policy per business unit, because an organization can hold any number of them

stem: Analytics VMs inside an enforced perimeter must write nightly export files to one Cloud Storage bucket that an external auditor owns in project audit-ext, outside the perimeter. The writes are denied with an egress violation. What is the narrowest fix?

choices.text: Remove Cloud Storage from the perimeter's restricted services so that every bucket can be written from any network
An access level for the auditor's address ranges attached to the perimeter, since an access level admits calls to outside buckets
Add audit-ext to the perimeter so that the auditor's bucket and the analytics projects share a single security boundary
An egress rule that lets the export service account call Cloud Storage object-creation methods on projects/audit-ext only

stem: Project corp-storage is in the enforced configuration of perimeter PA. The security team wants to find out what would break if it moved into perimeter PB, before changing any real protection. Which approach is correct?

choices.text: Remove the project from PA's dry run configuration, add it to PB's dry run configuration, review logs, then move it in enforced mode in the same order
Delete PA's enforced configuration, so that the project is unprotected while PB's dry run results are collected
Add the project to PB's dry run configuration while it stays in PA's dry run configuration, since a project can be in several dry run perimeters
Add the project to PB's enforced configuration first, then remove it from PA once no denials appear in the logs

stem: Two VPC networks, net-app and net-db, are peered. A security administrator of net-db wrote an ingress allow rule for port 5432 whose source is the network tag app-tier, expecting VMs in net-app that carry the same tag to connect. The connections time out. What is the cause, and the best fix?

choices.text: Peering does not carry internal traffic for TCP port 5432, so the database must be moved to a Cloud SQL private services access range
Network tags resolve only inside the rule's own network, so use the application subnet's IP range as the source or a secure tag in a network firewall policy
VPC Network Peering exchanges firewall rules between the networks, so the duplicate tag creates a conflict that blocks the connection
The rule needs a matching egress rule in net-app, because peered networks have an implied deny egress rule toward each other

stem: A security team worries that application owners might peer production VPC networks with networks of outside parties or unmanaged projects. They want a preventive control that applies to every project in the production folder, not detective monitoring. What should the engineer use?

choices.text: A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the folder, because perimeters block creation of peering connections between networks
A firewall policy that denies all ingress from private RFC 1918 ranges, which prevents peered traffic from being accepted
The VPC peering restriction constraint on the folder, with an allowlist of networks under the company organization
A Cloud Audit Logs alert on peering creation events, so that unapproved peerings are reviewed and removed afterwards

stem: A database tier lives in network net-db, and the application tier in the peered network net-app. The database team wants only application subnet 10.20.0.0/24 to reach tcp:5432, with the smallest rule set. Which configuration is sufficient?

choices.text: An ingress allow rule in net-db and an egress allow rule in net-app, because both directions need explicit permission across peering
Ingress rules in both networks that name each other's network tags, which lets the peering identify the matching tiers
One ingress allow rule in net-db for tcp:5432 with source 10.20.0.0/24, as net-app egress is already allowed by the implied rule
A single egress allow rule in net-app, because peering applies the firewall rules of the calling network to the callee

stem: A security team wants to prevent any VM in the production folder from being turned into a router that relays traffic between tiers around the planned firewall rules, except for VMs in one appliance project that runs approved virtual firewalls. Which control fits?

choices.text: Enforce the external IP restriction constraint on the folder, because VMs without public addresses cannot relay packets at all
Add a VPC firewall rule to every network that denies packets whose destination address is not the receiving VM's own address
Place the production projects in a VPC Service Controls perimeter, because perimeters block relaying of packets between VMs
Enforce the organization policy constraint that restricts VM IP forwarding on the folder, and override it for the appliance project only

stem: A company runs Shared VPC and wants separation of duties among network administrators, security administrators and service project teams. Which delegation is correct?

choices.text: Grant the Shared VPC Admin role to the security team, because that role is the one that creates and edits firewall rules
Grant the Security Admin role on the host project to the team that manages firewall rules and SSL certificates
Grant the Network Admin role on the host project to the network team, which gives full control of all network resources, including firewall rules
Grant Service Project Admins the Network Admin role on the host project so that they can create the subnets their VMs need

stem: A security team must write one rule at the organization level that blocks Telnet to all VMs. For SSH, project teams should decide for themselves, without the organization policy allowing or blocking it. Which rule actions in the hierarchical firewall policy fit?

choices.text: A deny rule for tcp:23 and a goto_next rule for tcp:22, so project-level rules decide SSH
An allow rule for tcp:22 and a deny rule for tcp:23, so that SSH passes and Telnet is blocked
A deny rule for tcp:22 and tcp:23, since lower levels can then override the SSH block with allow rules
A goto_next rule for tcp:23 and an allow rule for tcp:22, so that both are decided at the project level

stem: Remote analysts must query BigQuery in a project protected by an enforced perimeter from home networks whose IP addresses change often. Only devices that meet a security baseline (screen lock, storage encryption, supported operating system) should be accepted, even when the credentials are valid. Which design fits?

choices.text: An access level with a device policy fed by Endpoint Verification, used as the source of an ingress rule for the analyst group
A dry run configuration of the perimeter, because dry run mode refuses requests from devices that fail a security baseline
An access level listing the current home address ranges of every analyst, attached to the perimeter as its admission test
An egress rule from the perimeter toward the analysts' laptops, naming the analyst group as the identities that may connect

stem: A regulated company hosts a customer database tier in a project reachable only from the application tier. An egress firewall rule denies the data VMs everything except traffic to the Google API range, yet a red team shows that a compromised data VM can copy records to a Cloud Storage bucket in an attacker-controlled project. What design addition best addresses this?

choices.text: Apply a stricter ingress rule on the application tier, because the copy is initiated by the application tier from outside
Place the data projects in a VPC Service Controls perimeter, with API access from the VMs going through restricted Google API access and narrow egress rules
Allow egress only to storage.googleapis.com by hostname in VPC firewall rules, because the hostname identifies which bucket receives the data
Add more egress firewall deny rules that list the attacker's bucket name, because firewall rules can match individual bucket names

stem: A security team hardens new projects in a three-tier design with web, application and database VMs. Which TWO measures reduce risk from a default VPC network and enforce tier isolation? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Give the web tier an ingress allow rule for tcp:1433 from 0.0.0.0/0, because the database listens on that port
Allow all internal traffic with one broad rule on the whole VPC network, because tiers sit inside the same trust boundary
Enforce the constraint that skips default network creation, and build custom-mode VPC networks with only the subnets needed
Place all three tiers on one shared subnet and rely on the operating system firewall of each VM for isolation
Write allow rules by service account or secure tag for web to app and app to database only, with other ingress denied

stem: A bank protects a Cloud SQL and BigQuery estate with Cloud EKM keys that Google Cloud reaches over the internet. Operations see intermittent FAILED_PRECONDITION errors at peak load because the external key manager is slow to answer. Policy still requires the key material to stay in the bank's external key manager, and the data lives in one region. What should change?

choices.text: Replace the external keys with Cloud HSM keys in a multi-region location, so the key manager stays out of the request path
Create the external keys in the global location, which is the closest location to every external key manager partner
Cache the external key material in Cloud KMS for a short period, so repeated requests stop leaving Google Cloud
Use Cloud EKM over a VPC connection in that region, so the key manager is reached over a private network path

stem: A security team sets a 90-day automatic rotation schedule on a Cloud EKM key that was created by entering the key URI of an existing key in the external manager. The schedule is rejected. What explains this, and what would allow scheduled rotation?

choices.text: External keys need a rotation period above 365 days, so the schedule has to be lengthened and then rotated manually every quarter
Manually managed external keys cannot rotate automatically; use a coordinated key through an EKM-over-VPC connection managed from Cloud KMS
Rotation schedules apply only to software keys, so the key has to be recreated as a software key and the external manager dropped
Cloud EKM keys can be rotated only by Google Cloud Support, who must be asked to rotate on the agreed date

stem: A company evaluates Cloud EKM for regulated workloads. Which TWO statements about Cloud EKM are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The external key material is never cached or stored in Google Cloud, so an unreachable external key makes the protected operations fail
Cloud EKM keys can be created in the global location, so a single key can protect resources in every region
Cloud EKM keeps a copy of the key in Cloud KMS to decrypt data when the partner is down, until access is restored
Google Cloud Support can troubleshoot the external key manager directly, so no support contract with the partner is needed for it
Revoking the project's access in the external manager stops use of the key, and lost keys mean unrecoverable data

stem: A payment processor must show its auditor that the CMEK keys protecting cardholder data are generated and used inside FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware, with verifiable evidence for each key. It has no requirement to keep keys outside Google or to have exclusive hardware. Which key choice fits?

choices.text: Cloud EKM keys over the internet, so that an external hardware vendor supplies the compliance evidence for the keys
A Single-tenant Cloud HSM instance in every region, so that dedicated HSM partitions administered by the company carry the keys
Software protection level keys, since the validated module is FIPS 140-3 and the newer standard satisfies the hardware requirement
Cloud HSM keys at the multi-tenant HSM protection level, with each key's attestation statement and certificate chains given to the auditor

stem: A bucket uses a software Cloud KMS key as its default key. Compliance now demands hardware-protected keys, and an engineer tries to change the protection level of the existing key. It is refused. What is the correct path?

choices.text: Delete the key and create another with the same name at the HSM level, so that the bucket picks it up automatically on its next write
Add a new key version at the HSM protection level to the same key, then disable the old software version
Create a new HSM key in a location that supports Cloud HSM, make it the bucket default and rewrite existing objects
Export the software key material, then re-import it into the same key as a version at the HSM protection level

stem: After suspecting that an old version of a symmetric Cloud KMS key was exposed, an administrator rotated the key. Weeks later a red team shows the exposed version can still decrypt stored data. Which step was missed?

choices.text: Rotation only adds a primary version; data needed re-encrypting with it, and the old version disabling and then destruction
The old version had to be left alone, because versions expire automatically once the rotation period has elapsed
Rotation also had to be applied to the key ring, which re-keys every key it holds and removes the exposed versions from use
The key had to be deleted, because Cloud KMS then regenerates it and re-encrypts all protected data automatically

stem: A release pipeline signs firmware with a Cloud KMS asymmetric signing key. Policy requires replacing signing keys every 180 days, and an attempt to set an automatic rotation schedule on this key fails. Which approach meets the policy with the least risk of breaking device verification?

choices.text: Convert the key to a symmetric key, which supports automatic rotation, and verify firmware with the shared key
Create a new key version, publish its public key to verifiers, switch the pipeline to it, then disable the old version later
Keep the key as it is, because the private part never leaves Cloud KMS and so asymmetric keys are exempt from rotation policies
Schedule the current version for destruction on day 180 and let the pipeline fall back to the primary version of the key

stem: A SaaS vendor gives every tenant its own Cloud KMS key. Contracts say that after offboarding a tenant's data must become permanently unreadable within 7 days, while the security team wants a short window to undo mistakes. The default scheduled-for-destruction period is 30 days. Which design satisfies both?

choices.text: Lower the destruction period on every existing tenant key at offboarding, because the setting can be changed at any time after creation
Delete the tenant's key ring at offboarding, which destroys every key in it at once
Create each tenant key with a destruction period of a few days, then schedule destruction of its versions at offboarding
Disable the tenant key at offboarding, since disabled versions are destroyed automatically after seven days

stem: During a clean-up of Cloud KMS, an engineer disables the key version that protects a production Cloud SQL instance with CMEK. Minutes later the instance stops serving queries. What happened, and how is service restored?

choices.text: Cloud SQL deleted the instance's data files; recovery needs a restore from a backup encrypted with the same disabled key version
Cloud SQL switched to Google-managed encryption and failed over; restarting the instance returns it to the CMEK key
Only the service agent's IAM binding matters, so adding the Cloud KMS Admin role to the agent resumes the instance
Cloud SQL suspended the instance as it cannot use the key; re-enabling the version lets the instance resume

stem: A company generates AES keys in its on-premises HSM and must bring one into Cloud HSM. Which TWO statements about importing key material into Cloud KMS are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The imported key becomes a new version of an existing target key, and importing into a key that already has a version is not allowed
Once imported, the key material can be exported back to the on-premises HSM through a signed support request
Imported keys rotate automatically every 90 days, with new material generated on-premises through the import job
The protection level is set by the import job and key material cannot later be moved to a different storage environment
The key is wrapped locally with an import job's public key, and an import job expires after three days, so an expired one must be replaced

stem: A bank's policy says all key material for its Cloud HSM CMEK must originate in its own on-premises HSM, and Google must never generate it. It will bring in fresh material every quarter. How should the key be set up?

choices.text: Create a normal HSM key and enable 90-day automatic rotation, which pulls new material from the on-premises HSM on each cycle
Create the key with Google-generated version one, then import later versions and destroy version one right after the first import
Create an import-only key without an initial version, import each quarter's material as a new version, and leave automatic rotation off
Use Autokey on the folder, since it accepts customer-supplied material when each new key is requested

stem: A SaaS vendor must be able to crypto-shred a single tenant's data and allow each tenant's support group to use only that tenant's data. Today it has one Cloud KMS key with a new key version per tenant and grants groups encrypt and decrypt on the key. The architect says this cannot meet both goals. Why, and what is the fix?

choices.text: Access cannot be managed per key version, so a grant covers every enabled version; use one key per tenant in a shared key ring
The key needs to be asymmetric, because only asymmetric key versions can carry separate IAM policies for different groups
Disabling the whole key ring isolates a tenant, so the vendor should keep the single key and use a key ring per tenant
Each tenant key version can hold its own IAM policy only through IAM Conditions, so conditions on version names must be added

stem: A security team plans to roll out Cloud KMS Autokey and wants to know what it guarantees. Which TWO statements about keys created by Autokey are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A Cloud KMS administrator can switch an Autokey key from the HSM protection level to software once the team has validated the rollout
Each key is created in the same location as the resource it protects, and where Cloud HSM is unavailable the CMEK has to be created manually
Developers who create protected resources receive Cloud KMS Admin on the key project, so that they can view and rotate their own keys
Autokey keeps one global key ring and one key per service, which every region reuses so that no new key is created per location
A Cloud KMS administrator can view, disable and destroy these keys but is not given permission to encrypt or decrypt with them

stem: A company's data in Cloud Storage and BigQuery is already encrypted at rest with Google-managed keys. Which TWO requirements justify moving to customer-managed encryption keys in Cloud KMS? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An authorized analyst with read access must be stopped from seeing plaintext values, which CMEK blocks at query time
Data must be protected in transit between clients and Cloud Storage, which CMEK enforces on every connection
Data must be encrypted at rest at all, because Google-managed encryption does not apply to Cloud Storage and BigQuery
The company must control rotation schedule, key location and the audit trail of key use, and be able to disable the key
The company must be able to make data inaccessible quickly by disabling or destroying the key under its own control

stem: A data team publishes a view in the dataset reporting that exposes only non-sensitive columns of a table in the dataset raw_claims, which sits in the same region. Analysts hold BigQuery Data Viewer on reporting and the job user role on the project, and must not get access to raw_claims. Their queries on the view fail with an access denied error on the source table. What is missing?

choices.text: The analysts need the Fine-Grained Reader role on the view, so that the policy tags of its source columns are honored
The view must be moved into the raw_claims dataset, so that it inherits that dataset's access list for its readers
The view has not been authorized on the raw_claims dataset, so it cannot read the source table on behalf of analysts
The analysts need BigQuery Data Viewer on the raw_claims dataset as well, so that the view can read the table for them

stem: An audit found that the analyst group holds BigQuery Data Viewer at the project level, so it can read every dataset in the project, including payroll. Analysts should read only two curated datasets and run query jobs. Which change fixes this?

choices.text: Move the payroll datasets into a new folder, since IAM roles granted on a project do not apply to resources moved out
Remove the project-level Data Viewer, grant Data Viewer on the two datasets, and keep BigQuery Job User on the project
Keep the project-level role and add a row-level access policy to each payroll table that matches no analyst
Grant BigQuery User at the project level, which lets analysts run queries but not read table data on its own

stem: A central team maintains 40 views in the dataset published_views, built over three source datasets owned by different teams in the same region. Every new view means editing each source dataset's access list. The team wants one-time grants while analysts still cannot read the source tables. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Authorize the published_views dataset on each source dataset, so every view in it can read them
Grant analysts Data Viewer on the three source datasets, so the views work without any authorization
Authorize each new view individually on every source dataset, with the grants managed in a spreadsheet
Copy the needed tables into published_views every night, then give analysts access to the copies

stem: A nightly ingestion service account must add new log files to a Cloud Storage bucket. Even if its credentials are stolen, it must not be able to read, overwrite or delete existing objects. Which grant on the bucket fits?

choices.text: Storage Object Viewer together with the legacy bucket writer role, so creation is allowed and existing objects are read-only
Storage Admin limited by an IAM condition on the object name prefix, so only the log prefix is writable
Storage Object User, since it allows writing and the service can be trusted not to delete or read
Storage Object Creator, which allows creating objects but not viewing, deleting or overwriting them

stem: Security wants to ensure that no project in the production folder can expose bucket data to anonymous internet users or share it with identities outside the corporate domain. Which TWO organization policy constraints should be enforced on the folder? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The public access prevention constraint for Cloud Storage, so allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers cannot be granted access
The constraint that restricts non-CMEK services, so that buckets must use a customer-managed key
The resource locations constraint, set to the company's approved regions for all new resources
The uniform bucket-level access constraint, so that all buckets disable object ACLs
The domain restricted sharing constraint, allowing only the corporate customer ID in IAM policies

stem: Cloud Run services connect to a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance using database passwords kept in Secret Manager. The security team wants to remove long-lived database passwords and see in audit logs which workload identity logged in. What should they implement?

choices.text: Authorize the Cloud Run egress IP ranges on the instance and remove the passwords, since the network path then identifies the caller
Rotate the database passwords every hour with a Secret Manager schedule and keep one shared database user for all services
IAM database authentication for each service's service account, using a Cloud SQL connector, with the instance user and client roles granted
Issue one client certificate for all services and require it for every connection, so that the certificate identifies each workload

stem: The organization policy sql.restrictPublicIp was enforced at the organization last month. A scan today still finds three older Cloud SQL instances reachable through a public IP address. Why, and what is the next step?

choices.text: The constraint takes effect after each instance restart, so scheduling a restart of the three instances will remove the public IP
The constraint is not retroactive, so existing public IPs remain; move those instances to private IP and review their authorized networks
Organization policies take effect only after 30 days, so the instances will be updated automatically after that period
The constraint covers only new MySQL instances, so the PostgreSQL ones need a separate policy that has to be enforced

stem: A healthcare provider requires that secrets for its German clinic systems stay in the Frankfurt region at rest, in use and in transit, and are readable only by workloads there. The team uses global secrets with automatic replication. Which design fits best?

choices.text: Keep global secrets and place the Secret Manager API inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter, so data is bound to the perimeter
Keep global secrets and encrypt them with a customer-managed key in Frankfurt, so the data stays in Germany
Keep global secrets and enforce the resource locations constraint for Germany, so the replication policy only chooses German regions
Use regional secrets in the Frankfurt location, accessed through the regional service by workloads running in that location

stem: A payment service reads the db-password secret using the latest alias at startup. A rotation job added a faulty version, the autoscaler launched new instances that crashed on start, and the service went down. Which practice prevents a repeat?

choices.text: Grant the service Secret Manager Secret Version Manager so it can disable a faulty version and roll itself back
Destroy older versions right after each new one is added, so only a single version can ever be read
Pin deployments to explicit version numbers, roll new numbers out normally, and disable (not destroy) old versions first
Copy the latest value into an environment variable at build time, so that startup no longer depends on Secret Manager being reachable

stem: A team configures a 30-day rotation period and a Pub/Sub topic on an API-key secret in Secret Manager. After 30 days the topic shows a published message, but no new secret version exists and the application still uses the old key. What is missing?

choices.text: A subscriber must act on the SECRET_ROTATE message, create the new credential at the provider and add a new secret version
Rotation only works if the schedule is set on every version, so the period has to be copied onto each existing version
The secret needs the latest alias removed, since Secret Manager cannot add a version while that alias exists
Secret Manager must be switched to customer-managed encryption first, because rotation messages are only sent for CMEK secrets

stem: A public web app on Compute Engine fetches user-supplied URLs. A penetration test shows an attacker can make it call the metadata server and obtain the VM service account's access token. Which TWO measures best limit this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Rotate the VM service account's keys every 24 hours, so a stolen token expires before it can be used
Run the VM as a dedicated user-managed service account that holds only the roles the application needs
Disable Private Google Access on the VM's subnet so that metadata requests no longer reach the server
Enable OS Login on the VM, so that metadata server requests need an authenticated operating system user
Block the app's outbound requests to the metadata hostname and link-local address, and sandbox the URL-fetching component

stem: A platform team passes a database password to VMs as a custom metadata key that the startup script reads. A security review flags the practice. What is the concern, and what is the fix?

choices.text: Any process in the VM and any viewer of the instance can read custom metadata, so keep it in Secret Manager and fetch it with the VM's identity
Metadata values are written unencrypted to the boot disk, so the fix is a customer-managed key on the boot disk
Startup scripts always run as root, so the fix is to read the password in a shutdown script that runs with fewer privileges
Metadata values are visible to every project in the organization, so the fix is an organization policy that restricts metadata access to named owners

stem: Developers hold Compute Instance Admin and can edit project metadata. An incident showed that someone added an SSH key to project-wide metadata, gaining login on every VM in the project. Security wants SSH access governed by IAM and no key distribution through metadata. Which control fits?

choices.text: Remove external IP addresses from all VMs, since instances without public IPs cannot be reached by SSH keys
Enforce the Require OS Login constraint and grant OS Login roles to groups, so metadata SSH keys stop being accepted
Rotate the project-wide SSH key in metadata every day and keep the public key list reviewed by the security team
Block project-wide SSH keys on each VM by hand and ask teams to keep the setting on new instances

stem: Pods on a GKE cluster obtain credentials from the Compute Engine metadata server, so a compromised pod could call Google APIs with the node service account's permissions. The team wants each workload to hold only its own identity. Which design achieves this?

choices.text: Grant the node service account the union of every workload's roles, so any pod works without extra setup
Export a service account key for each workload and mount it as a Kubernetes Secret, so pods stop using the node's identity
Place workloads in separate namespaces and rely on namespace boundaries to stop pods from reaching the node's metadata server and its tokens
Enable Workload Identity Federation for GKE with the GKE metadata server on node pools, then grant IAM roles to the Kubernetes principals
